terms.comment: Classically the army’s cloth banner, a diminutive of vēlum (Lewis & Short; de Vaan 660). Traupman uses it for a national flag (p. 27) and gives vexillum quassāre, to wave a flag (p. 404).

phrases.english: The flag is flapping in the wind.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 27, 316, 404. Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), p. 660, s.v. vēlum. Morgan–Owens has only the royal standard, vexillum rēgāle; Levi–Bini has no entry.
